Some people have argued that the man in this photo is not Hiroshi Ouchi. See this reddit thread, specifically these comments.

I wish someone would update snopes or something with this image. This image is not of Ouchi. I have the book written about Ouchi called "A Slow Death: 83 Days of Radiation Sickness", and it contains pictures of Ouchi as well as the hospital he was housed in. None of the pictures resemble this place or the body in this picture. The association of this image with Ouchi is an internet fabrication.

Also:

The picture at 2:01 isn't in the book, although the picture before that one is (of the arm). The main reason I'm skeptical that OP's image is of Ouchi is because all the pictures of his hospital room in the book make it look like a small, clean room. Not a fucking nightmare dungeon. Also there is no record of amputation in the very detailed account of Ouchi's ordeal in the book, whereas the person in OP's picture is missing both feet. Finally, the book details how the skin which faced the immediate radiation exposure was red and looked burned/scalded, but the skin on the reverse side of his body did not. Basically, lots of things don't add up to allow one to conclude that this is a picture of Ouchi. The curious thing, though, is that basically every result of a reverse-image-search of the picture lead to stories about Ouchi. However, none of the sites are particularly reputable and I didn't see any dating back earlier than 2011ish. The same goes for the back picture in the video you posted. I found some sites that linked the image to the same accident that Ouchi was in, but were accompanied by a picture of another man (not ouchi) and it says the person died after 211 days (Ouchi died after 83). So, since the accident that Ouchi was in had another fatality besides him, it's possible that the photo is of the other man who died from radiation sickness as a result of the same accident. But who knows, I tend to think the association between these photos and those deaths are inventions.
